NONE: › always being pleasant
平和的；性情溫和的
› not changing suddenly
穩定的，變化小的

example: Graham has a fairly equable temperament - I haven't often seen him really angry.
格雷厄姆性情很平和——我不怎麽見他真正動肝火。
The south of the country enjoys an equable climate.
這個國家的南部地區氣候溫和穩定。

NONE: B1 the same in amount, number, or size
（數量、大小）相同的，相等的
B1 the same in importance and deserving the same treatment
（地位、待遇）平等的，同等的

after verb: › [ after verb ] formal skilled or brave enough for a difficult duty or piece of work
（能力、勇氣）勝任的，合適的，相當的

NONE: B2 someone or something that has the same importance as someone or something else and deserves the same treatment
（應獲得同等待遇的）同等重要的人或物

L only + noun, T: › to be the same in value or amount as something else
與某物（質量或數量）相等
› to achieve the same standard or level as someone else, or the same standard or level as you did before
達到（他人或自己過去的）相同標準或水準

example: One litre is equal to 1.76 imperial pints.
1升等於1.76 英製品脫。
One box may look bigger than the other, but in fact they are roughly (= almost) equal in volume.
一個盒子可能看起來比另一個大，但其實它們的容量大致相等。
All people are equal, deserving the same rights as each other.
所有人都是平等的，享有同等的權利。
They've got a long way to go before they achieve equal pay/status for men and women.
要實現男女同工同酬／地位平等，他們仍有很長的路要走。
It's a challenging job but I'm sure you'll prove equal to it.
這項工作很有挑戰性，但是我相信你最終有能力完成它。
Is he equal to the task?
他能勝任這項任務嗎？
The good thing about her as a boss is that she treats us all as equals.
作爲老闆，她的優點就在於她對待我們一視同仁。
Throughout her marriage she never considered her husband as her intellectual equal.
自結婚之日起，她一直就認爲在才智上她丈夫根本無法和她相提並論。
As an all-round athlete he has no equal (= no-one else is as good).
他作爲一名全能運動員，無人可望其項背。
16 ounces equals one pound.
16盎司等於1磅。
We raised over $500 for charity last year and we're hoping to equal that this year.
去年我們籌得的善款超過500美元，今年我們希望可以跟去年做得一樣好。
He disputed the idea that more money equals better education.
他質疑更多的投資會帶來更好的教育這一觀點。

NONE: › marriage between two people of the same sex, thought of as being legally the same as, and of equal importance to, marriage between two people of opposite sexes
婚姻平權（指同性婚姻與異性婚姻在法律上享有同等權利並且同等重要的觀點）

example: He argued that equal marriage legislation would create a more tolerant society.
他的觀點是婚姻平權立法將幫助建立一個更加包容的社會。

NONE: › the principle of treating all people the same, and not being influenced by a person's sex, race, religion, etc.
機會均等

example: The advert said "We are an equal opportunities employer".
徵人廣告寫著「我們的用人原則：人人機會均等」。

NONE: › a principle included in the 14th amendment of the US Constitution that says all people must be treated equally by the law
（美國憲法第十四修正案的）平等保護條款
› the symbol =, used to show that two things are the same in value, size, meaning, etc.
等號（＝）
B2 the right of different groups of people to have a similar social position and receive the same treatment
（社會地位、待遇上的）平等；均等

example: racial equality
種族平等
the government department responsible for equalities
負責平等問題的政府機構

T: › [ T ] to make things or people equal
I: › [ I ] UK to get the point in a game or competition that makes your score the same as that of the other team or player

example: They are putting pressure on the government to equalize state pension ages between men and women.
他們正在向政府施壓，希望在國家老人年金發放的年齡問題上實現男女平等。
Spain managed to equalize in the last minute of the game.
西班牙隊在比賽的最後一分鐘將比分扳平。

C: › the point in a game or competition that gives both teams or players the same score

example: He scored an equalizer during the closing minutes of the game.
在比賽的最後幾分鐘裡他進球將比分扳平。

NONE: B2 fairly and in the same way
平等地；相同地
C1 in equal amounts
平均；均等
C1 to the same degree
同樣地；相等地；相同地；均等地
› used for adding an idea that is as important as what you have just said
同樣地…（用於加入一個與前面所說內容同樣重要的觀點）

example: In an ideal world, would everyone get treated equally?
在理想世界裡，每個人都會得到平等待遇嗎？
The inheritance money was shared equally among the three sisters.
遺産的錢由三姐妹均分。
You looked equally nice in both dresses.
這兩件連衣裙你穿哪件都一樣漂亮。
Not all businesses are legitimate. Equally, not all customers are honest.
不是所有的生意都是合法的。同樣地，不是所有的顧客都是誠實的。

NONE: › a calm mental state, especially after a shock or disappointment or in a difficult situation
（尤指處於震驚、失望或困境時的）鎮靜，沈著，冷靜

example: He received the news of his mother's death with remarkable equanimity.
他接到母親去世的噩耗時表現得異常鎮靜。
Three years after the tragedy she has only just begun to regain her equanimity.
悲劇已經過去三年了，她才剛剛開始恢復心情的平靜。

NONE: C2 to consider one thing to be the same as or equal to another thing
同等看待；使等同；使相等

example: He complained that there was a tendency to equate right-wing politics with self-interest.
他抱怨說，人們往往會把右翼政見和自私自利混爲一談。

NONE: › to be the same in amount, number, or size
相當於；等於

example: The price of such goods in those days equates to about $50 at current prices.
那個時候這類商品的價格大概相當於現價50美元。

C: C1 [ C ] a mathematical statement in which you show that two amounts are equal using mathematical symbols
› [ C ] also chemical equation a statement containing chemical symbols, used to show the changes that happen during a particular chemical reaction

C usually singular: › [ C usually singular ] a difficult problem that can only be understood if all the different influences are considered

U: › [ U ] the act of considering one thing to be the same as or equal to another

example: Managing the economy is a complex equation of controlling inflation and reducing unemployment.
經濟管理包括控制通貨膨脹、降低失業率等複雜的因素。
There is a tendency in movies to make the equation between violence and excitement.
電影傾向於把暴力和刺激畫上等號。

NONE: › an imaginary line drawn around the middle of the earth an equal distance from the North Pole and the South Pole
赤道

example: Indonesia is/lies on the equator.
印尼位於赤道之上。

NONE: › near the equator, or typical of places near the equator
赤道的；赤道附近的

example: The equatorial climate of the Amazonian rain forests is hot and wet.
亞馬遜雨林的赤道氣候炎熱潮濕。

NONE: › a country in West Africa
赤道幾內亞（西非國家）
› belonging to or relating to Equatorial Guinea
赤道幾內亞的
› a person from Equatorial Guinea
赤道幾內亞人
› an officer who works for a particular member of a royal family to help in their official duties
（英國）王室侍從武官

example: an equerry to the Queen
女王的侍從武官

NONE: › connected with the riding of horses
騎馬的；騎術的
› a person who rides horses, especially as a job or very skilfully
（尤指職業的或技術精湛的）騎馬者，騎師，馬術家

example: They plan to hold the Olympics' equestrian events in another part of the city.
他們計劃將奧運會馬術比賽項目安排在該市的另一個地區舉行。

NONE: › equal or equally
相等的（地）
› equally far or close
等距的

example: Australia is roughly equidistant from Africa and South America.
澳大利亞離非洲和南美洲的距離大致相等。

NONE: › used to describe a shape whose sides are all the same length
等邊的

example: an equilateral triangle
等邊三角形

NONE: › a force that is able to balance a system of forces
平衡力
› a state of balance
平衡；均衡
› a calm mental state
（心情或情緒的）平靜，安寧；心理平衡

example: The disease destroys much of the inner ear, disturbing the animal's equilibrium.
這種疾病破壞動物內耳的大部分組織，妨礙其保持均衡。
the country's economic equilibrium
該國經濟的均衡發展
Yoga is said to restore one's inner equilibrium.
據說練瑜伽可以使人恢復內心的平靜。

NONE: › connected with horses, or appearing similar to a horse
馬的；似馬的

example: The portraits showed an aristocratic family with long equine faces.
這是一套貴族家庭的畫像，所有人都長著長長的馬臉。

NONE: › either of the two occasions in the year when day and night are of equal length
晝夜平分時；春分；秋分

example: the vernal/autumn equinox
春／秋分

T: B2 to provide a person or a place with objects that are necessary for a particular purpose
› to give someone the skills needed to do a particular thing
使有準備；使有能力；訓練

example: It's going to cost $4 million to equip the hospital.
給這所醫院配齊醫療設備將耗資400萬美元。
All the police officers were equipped with shields to defend themselves against the rioters.
所有警察都配備了盾牌以便在與暴亂分子的對抗中防身。

本課程旨在使人們獲得在這個科技時代必備的工作技能。
A degree in the history of art is very nice but it doesn't exactly equip you for many jobs.
能獲得一個藝術史學位固然不錯，但在很多工作中它並不見得會使你有用武之地。

NONE: B1 the set of necessary tools, clothing, etc. for a particular purpose
設備；器材；用具
› formal the act of equipping a person or place
裝備；配備

example: office/camping/kitchen equipment
辦公設備／野營用具／廚房用具
electrical equipment
電器設備

NONE: C1 having the necessary tools, clothes, equipment, etc.
配有必要的工具（衣物、設備等）的；裝備齊全的

+ to infinitive: › [ + to infinitive ] having the skills needed to do something
有能力的；受過（專業）訓練的

example: Their schools are very poorly equipped.
他們學校的教學設備很簡陋。
We were well equipped for the trip.
那次旅行，我們都裝備齊全。

很多人都認爲他是最有條件當總統的一位領袖。
Not being a specialist in the subject I don't feel very well-equipped to answer such questions.
我不是這一學科的專家，所以我覺得我不太有資格回答這樣的問題。

NONE: › treating everyone fairly and in the same way
公平合理的；公正的

example: an equitable tax system
合理的稅收制度

C or U: › [ C or U ] specialized finance & economics the value of a company, divided into many equal parts owned by the shareholders, or one of the equal parts into which the value of a company is divided
U: › [ U ] the value of a property after you have paid any mortgage or other charges relating to it
› [ U ] formal the situation in which everyone is treated fairly and equally
› [ U ] specialized law in English-speaking countries, a system of justice that allows a fair judgment of a case where the laws that already exist are not satisfactory
（英語國家的一種司法制度，允許在現存法律不適用時對案件作出公正判決的）衡平法

example: He sold his equity in the company last year.
他去年賣掉了這家公司的股票。
The rights give holders the opportunity to purchase additional equity interests in the company at a big discount.
這些權利使得股票持有者有機會以很優惠的折扣價額外購買該公司股份。
a society based on equity and social justice
建立在公平公正和社會公義基礎之上的社會

NONE: C1 having the same amount, value, purpose, qualities, etc.
等值的；相等的；等同的
C1 something that has the same amount, value, purpose, qualities, etc. as something else
等值；相等；等同

example: She's doing the equivalent job in the new company but for more money.
她在新公司做同樣的工作，但薪水比以前高。
There is no English equivalent for "bon appetit" so we have adopted the French expression.
英語中沒有和 bon appetit 相對應的詞，所以我們就借用了法語的這個表達方式。
Ten thousand people a year die of the disease - that's the equivalent of the population of this town.
每年有一萬人死於這種疾病——相當於這個城鎮的總人口。

NONE: › not clear and seeming to have two opposing meanings, or confusing and able to be understood in two different ways
含糊的；模棱兩可的；有歧義的

example: His words to the press were deliberately equivocal - he didn't deny the reports but neither did he confirm them.
他對新聞界發言時故意含糊其詞——既沒有否認也沒有證實這些報道。
Opposite
unequivocal

NONE: › to speak in a way that is intentionally not clear and confusing to other people, especially to hide the truth
（尤指爲隱瞞真相而）說模稜兩可的話，含糊其詞

example: She accused the minister of equivocating, claiming that he had deliberately avoided telling the public how bad the problem really was.
她指責部長含糊其詞，稱他故意不讓大眾知道問題真正嚴重到了甚麽地步。
